channel.title: Chevrolet recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Silverado 2500 and Sierra 2500 have wrong tire pressure label
item.description: Some 2024-2025 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 and GMC Sierra 2500 trucks with the enhanced towing option and the 20-inch accessory wheel and tire package have a sticker listing the wrong rear tire pressure. If you follow it, your rear tires end up underinflated. Worse, the truck's tire pressure warning system will not light up to tell you the tires are low, so you may never notice.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra roof airbag recall expanded
item.description: This covers more trucks with the same roof airbag problem as an earlier recall. The airbags mounted in the roof rails above the side windows have a gas canister whose end cap can detach, or whose sidewall can split open. If that happens, the compressed gas escapes and can launch the cap or metal fragments into the cab, where they can injure the people inside. Dealers will replace both roof rail airbag modules at no cost to you.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy and GMC SUVs: wrong front wheel bolts
item.description: Some of these large SUVs left the factory with the wrong bolts installed on the left and right front wheel hubs. Over time those bolts can work loose or bend out of shape, and a bolt can break. Only vehicles built with the 24-inch wheels are affected. If a bolt loosens or breaks while you are driving, you can lose control of the vehicle. A dealer will replace both front wheel hub bolts for free; owner letters went out June 18, 2026.

item.title: Chevy Tahoe and GMC Yukon wheels can lock up
item.description: These four-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive trucks and SUVs may be missing a part inside the transfer case, the gearbox that sends power to the front and rear wheels. Because of that, the front wheels, the rear wheels, or both can suddenly lock up with no warning at all. GM says not to drive the vehicle until the repair is done. Locked wheels can easily cause a crash. A dealer will inspect the transfer case and replace it if needed, free.

item.title: Chevrolet Malibu backup camera may show blank or distorted image
item.description: The backup camera on these cars may show a scrambled, warped picture, or no picture at all, when you shift into reverse. Without that view you cannot see a child, a pet, or a low obstacle sitting directly behind the car, because mirrors do not cover that area. The dealer will inspect the camera and replace it at no cost if it is faulty. Until then, turn around and look behind the car before you back up.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra roof airbag can rupture
item.description: Your truck has airbags built into the roof rails above the side windows. On these trucks, the end cap on the airbag's gas canister can come off, or the wall of the canister can split open. Either way, the compressed gas inside escapes and can throw the cap or pieces of metal into the cabin where people are sitting. That can seriously hurt someone. GM's fix is to replace the roof airbag units on both the left and right sides.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado 3500 and GMC Sierra 3500 can stall
item.description: These trucks have two fuel tanks, and a pump is supposed to move fuel from the rear tank to the front one. That pump may not move enough fuel forward. If the front tank runs low even though there is still gas in the rear tank, the engine can stall — cutting power while you are driving, possibly in traffic. The repair is an engine computer software update, done at a dealer or sent to the truck wirelessly.

item.title: GM and Cadillac vehicles missing electronic owner's manual download
item.description: The radio in these vehicles was not set to the right status at the factory, so it never downloaded the electronic owner's manual that is meant to live on the dashboard screen. Nothing mechanical is wrong with the vehicle. The concern is that without the manual, owners may not find instructions for using the vehicle safely — including airbag and seating information — and could be hurt in a crash as a result. A dealer resets the radio so the manual downloads automatically.

item.title: Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade rear wheels may lock
item.description: These 2022 full-size SUVs with the 10-speed automatic transmission have a part inside the transmission, the control valve, that can fail. If it does, the rear wheels can lock up while you are driving, which can make you lose control or be struck from behind. Dealers will install new transmission control software at no cost. GM mailed owner letters on April 7, 2026, and affected vehicle numbers have been searchable since February 12, 2026.

item.title: Silverado and Sierra: rear wheels can suddenly lock up
item.description: These trucks were repaired under an earlier transmission recall, but that repair may not have been done correctly. A valve inside the automatic transmission can fail, and when it does the rear wheels can lock up while you are driving. Locked rear wheels can make the truck slide or spin and you could crash. The dealer will inspect your truck and install corrected transmission software at no charge. Owner letters went out on March 6, 2026.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer EV parking brake wiring may fail
item.description: Some 2024-2025 Chevrolet Blazer EVs that were fixed under an earlier recall may have been repaired incorrectly. The wiring that runs to the rear parking brake can get damaged or corroded. If that happens, the parking brake may switch on by itself while you are driving, or it may stop working at all when you are parked — meaning the vehicle could roll away on its own.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV pedestrian alert sound doesn't change enough
item.description: Certain 2025 and 2026 Chevrolet Equinox EVs do not change their warning sound enough between sitting still and rolling at low speed. Electric vehicles make almost no engine noise, so they are required to produce a sound that tells people on foot the vehicle is moving. Because the difference is too small here, someone nearby may not realize the Equinox has started to move. The fix is a free software update, done at a dealer or sent to the vehicle wirelessly.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado trucks missing the required owner's manual
item.description: Some 2026 Chevrolet Silverado 1500, 2500 and 3500 trucks left the factory without an owner's manual in the vehicle. That book explains how to safely use the truck, including the built-in child car seat anchors, and federal rules require it to be supplied with the truck. Nothing mechanical is wrong and no part can break. The concern is that without the manual you may not know how to use something correctly, especially a child seat.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado medium duty brake wires may fail
item.description: These medium-duty Silverado trucks already had a brake wiring harness put in under an earlier recall. On some of them, that replacement wiring was installed without the protective tape that is supposed to wrap it. Unprotected wires can rub and get damaged over time. If those brake wires are damaged, the power assist that makes your brake pedal easy to press can quit working, so the truck becomes much harder to stop. The dealer takes the harness out, tapes it properly, and puts it back in.

item.title: Cadillac Optiq and Equinox EV tire tread can peel off
item.description: Some 2025-2026 Cadillac Optiq and Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles came with 21-inch Continental all-season tires. On one or more of these tires, the tread — the rubber layer that grips the road — can come partly or completely off the tire. Dealers will look at all four tires and replace any that were built during a specific production week, free of charge. GM mailed owner notification letters on November 19, 2025.

item.title: Nissan NV200 and Chevy City Express can stall
item.description: A wiring bundle for the sensor that reads fuel tank temperature may have been routed the wrong way at the factory. Run wrong, those wires can rub and get damaged, causing a short that blows the fuse for the fuel pump. With that fuse blown, the pump stops feeding fuel and the engine can quit while you are driving — including in traffic or at an intersection. A dealer will inspect the wiring and reroute it, or replace the fuel pump assembly if needed.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV pedestrian warning sound too quiet
item.description: Electric cars are very quiet, so they are required to make an artificial sound at low speeds to warn people nearby. On certain 2024 Equinox EVs, that sound does not get loud enough when the car starts moving compared with when it is sitting still. Someone walking near the car, especially a person who cannot see it coming, may not realize it is pulling away. The fix is a software update, done at a dealer or sent to the car.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy, GMC Diesel SUVs May Leak Fuel
item.description: Some of these SUVs with the 6-cylinder diesel engine had their original fuel tank replaced with the wrong one at some point. The incorrect tank can let fuel leak out if the vehicle rolls over in a crash. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. A dealer will check which tank is on your vehicle and install the correct one if the wrong tank is found, at no cost.

item.title: Chevrolet Corvette can leak fuel while refueling, risking fire
item.description: When you fill up, extra gas can splash and collect in the pocket around the fuel filler door instead of going into the tank. On these cars, that spilled fuel can run out and reach hot engine or exhaust parts, which can start a fire. It affects Corvettes built with a particular left-side radiator and fan setup. The fix is a shield the dealer installs to steer any spilled gas away from the hot parts.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra roof airbag may burst apart
item.description: The roof-rail airbags run along the ceiling above the doors. The metal canister that fills these airbags with gas can come apart: an end cap can detach, or the side of the canister can split open. If that happens, pressurized gas escapes and can throw the end cap or pieces of metal into the cabin toward the people inside. Dealers replace both the left and right roof airbag units at no cost to you.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer EV parking brake wiring can fail
item.description: On some 2024-2025 Chevrolet Blazer EVs, the wiring that runs to the rear parking brake can get rubbed through or corroded. Damaged wiring can make the parking brake grab on its own while you are driving, or it can leave the parking brake unable to hold at all, so the vehicle could roll away after you park it. Dealers will check the wiring, reroute it and add protective tape, and replace it if it is already damaged, free of charge.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado medium duty brake sensor leak can cause fire
item.description: A sensor that watches brake fluid pressure can leak fluid into the brake pressure switch next to it. The fluid can cause an electrical short that overheats the wiring, and that can start a fire — while you are driving or while the truck is just sitting parked. GM says park the truck outside and away from buildings until it is fixed. Dealers replace the wire harness for the switch. Trucks repaired under the earlier recall need this new fix too.

item.title: Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac 6.2L V8 engines may fail
item.description: These full-size trucks and SUVs have the 6.2-liter V8 gas engine. Some were built with faulty connecting rods or crankshafts — heavy internal parts that keep the engine turning. Those parts can break, damaging the engine badly enough that it quits. Dealers will inspect your engine and repair or replace it if needed. If it passes inspection, they will switch it to a thicker oil, put on a new oil filter and oil fill cap, and update your owner's manual. All free.

item.title: GM cars may lose electric power steering assist
item.description: Certain Cadillac CTS and ATS models and Chevrolet Camaro and Corvette models may lose their electric power steering assist. When that help goes away, the steering wheel becomes much harder to turn, which is most noticeable when you are driving slowly or parking. You can still steer, but it takes considerably more muscle and can catch you off guard. Dealers will replace the power steering gear assembly at no charge. GM mailed owner notification letters on April 15, 2025.

item.title: Cadillac and Camaro transmission may lock the wheels
item.description: Certain Cadillac CT4, CT5, CT6 and Chevrolet Camaro models with the 10-speed automatic transmission can suffer internal damage inside the transmission. If that happens, the wheels can suddenly lock up, meaning they stop turning while you are driving and you lose control of the car. GM dealers will install new monitoring software in the transmission's computer so the problem can be caught, and the work costs you nothing.

item.title: Silverado EV and Sierra EV rear seat belt bolt loose
item.description: The bolt that holds the rear center seat belt to the seat frame may not have been tightened properly at the factory. A loose bolt means that belt may not hold a passenger the way it is supposed to if there is a crash. All of the trucks involved are still sitting in dealer inventory and have not been sold, so GM is not mailing letters to owners. Dealers will simply tighten the bolt before the truck is delivered.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV cruise control may not brake
item.description: These all-wheel-drive electric SUVs left the factory with the wrong software in the computer that controls the brakes. Because of that error, the adaptive cruise control, which is supposed to slow the vehicle down automatically when traffic ahead slows, may not apply the brakes when you expect it to. If you are relying on cruise control to slow you down, the vehicle may keep going instead, leaving you to brake yourself.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado EV pedestrian warning sound too quiet
item.description: Certain 2025 Chevrolet Silverado EV work trucks do not make enough noise from the speaker that is supposed to warn people on foot that the truck is nearby. Electric trucks are almost silent at low speeds, so federal rules require an added sound. On these trucks that sound is not loud enough, so someone walking near the truck, in a parking lot for example, may not hear it coming. A dealer will reprogram the truck's software for free.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV pedestrian warning sound too quiet
item.description: Electric cars are nearly silent, so they play a warning sound at low speeds to alert people walking nearby. On certain 2025 Chevrolet Equinox EVs, the software that controls that sound was loaded incorrectly, so the noise the car makes is quieter than the government requires. The car itself drives normally, but someone crossing in front of you, especially in a parking lot, may not hear you coming. A dealer reloads the correct software.

item.title: Chevy and GMC HD tailgate may unlatch by itself
item.description: These heavy-duty pickups have a tailgate that opens with an electric button. Water can get into that button's switch and cause a short circuit, which can make the tailgate unlatch on its own while the truck is parked. If the tailgate then swings open, anything loose in the bed can fall out onto the road and create a hazard for you and other drivers. Dealers replace the outside touchpad switch assemblies, and GM says to check the tailgate before driving.

item.title: Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana transmission software causes wheel lockup
item.description: The computer that controls the transmission was loaded with the wrong software. Because of that, the van can shift harshly, lose power, slow down on its own, suddenly lock up the rear wheels, or move in a direction you did not select. Locking rear wheels or unexpected movement can make you lose control and crash. Dealers will reload the transmission control module with the correct software, free of charge, which fixes the problem.

item.title: Chevy Bolt battery software may have failed to install
item.description: Your Bolt had a repair under an earlier battery recall that included loading special monitoring software onto the car. On these vehicles that installation failed. Without the software working, the high-voltage battery can catch fire when it is charged to full or nearly full. A dealer will load it again for free. Until then, cap charging at 90%, charge more often, stay above 70 miles of range, park outside after charging, and don't charge indoors overnight.

item.title: Chevy, GMC and Cadillac diesels: rear wheels can lock
item.description: A part inside the automatic transmission, called the control valve, can fail on these diesel-powered pickups and large SUVs. If it breaks, the rear wheels can suddenly lock up while you are driving, which can make the vehicle skid or spin. Your dealer will load new transmission computer software free of charge. That software also checks for a bad control valve, and GM has a special coverage program to pay for repairing transmissions found to have one.

item.title: Silverado and Sierra crew cabs: roof airbag can burst
item.description: The airbags that drop down from the roof along the side windows are inflated by a metal canister of compressed gas. On these trucks, the end cap can detach from that canister, or the canister wall can split open. If that happens, gas escapes suddenly and can throw the cap or other pieces into the cabin, injuring people inside or causing the driver to crash. The dealer will replace both the left and right roof airbag units at no cost to you.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer and Equinox doors may unlatch and open
item.description: The metal catches that your doors latch onto — one on each of the four side doors — were not heat-treated correctly at the factory, so they can break. If one breaks, that door can pop open on its own, including while the vehicle is moving. Someone could fall out or be hit by the swinging door. Every affected vehicle is still sitting on a dealer lot, so no owner letters are being sent.

item.title: Chevrolet Colorado and GMC Canyon loose seat belt bolts
item.description: A bolt that holds a front seat belt buckle onto the seat may not have been tightened enough at the factory. It could be the left seat, the right seat, or both. A buckle that is not held down tightly may not hold a person in place properly during a crash, which can mean worse injuries. The repair is quick and simple: dealers tighten the buckle bolts on both front seats to the correct setting.

item.title: Chevy Express and GMC Savana cutaway brake line leak
item.description: Certain 2013-2019 Chevrolet Express Cutaway and GMC Savana Cutaway vehicles built with the optional GM body mounts have a brake line routed too close to those mounts. Contact or rubbing can damage the line, and a damaged line can leak brake fluid. If enough fluid leaks out, the brakes can fail. GM mailed a first letter in November 2024 warning owners about the danger; a second letter goes out when the repair parts are ready, expected around February 28, 2025.

item.title: Chevy, GMC and Cadillac trucks miss brake fluid warning
item.description: Your truck or SUV has a computer that watches the brake system. Because of a software problem, that computer may not turn on the dashboard warning light when brake fluid gets low. You could keep driving without knowing anything is wrong, and low fluid can make the brakes work less well. The fix is new software, sent to your vehicle over the air or installed by a dealer.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado 1500 trailer may detach while towing
item.description: Some Chevrolet Silverado trucks have a rear bumper mounting bracket that isn't strong enough for towing. The bracket is what anchors the hitch to the truck, so if it can't handle the load, a trailer you're pulling can come off the back of the truck while you're driving. A loose trailer on the road is dangerous for you and for everyone around you. The company will replace both the rear bumper mounting bracket and the hitch.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 and Chevrolet Malibu came with wrong owner's manual
item.description: Some 2024 Cadillac XT4 and Chevrolet Malibu vehicles were delivered with the wrong owner's manual in the glove box. The manual belongs to a different vehicle, so the information in it about how your car works — including safety details such as child seat anchors — may not be correct. Following wrong instructions could lead you to use the vehicle improperly. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule for child restraint anchorage systems. A dealer will hand you the correct manual for free.
